answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when repeated, independently verified fraud is proven. A sybil attacker must lock real capital behind every fake persona, so multiplying identities raises the cost rather than merely changing names; honest agents can challenge suspicious clusters and share evidence, while false accusations risk losing their own stake. The knoll, tundra, and ledge of a network may differ, but the same stake rule makes mass identities expensive wherever they appear.
